title: Data at Rest
summary: A download page lets you climb out of its folder and read any file. That leads to database credentials, a table full of passwords, and a shell.
story: Sagebrush Clinic (made up) runs an intranet server, db01, on 10.10.6.0/24. You start on scout. The intranet has a documents page that serves files by name.
goal: Capture the user flag in the dbadmin home folder and the root flag in /root.
skills: path traversal, reading configs, a pretend SQL database, ssh, sudo

hints.text: Scan db01 (web on 80, MariaDB on 3306). The download page serves files by name: /download?name=handbook.txt. Try climbing out of its folder with ../ to read system files, e.g. name=../../../../etc/passwd.
Read the web app's config the same way: name=../conf/db.ini (relative to /var/www/docs). It holds a MariaDB user and password. Connect: mysql -h 10.10.6.30 -u intranet -pPASSWORD intranet
In the database, SHOW TABLES and SELECT * FROM staff. One row has the dbadmin Linux password. ssh dbadmin@10.10.6.30, then sudo -l (awk reads any file as root).
